model: metadata-first knowledge modules with lazy references
setup_exception: agent-collaboration-setup uses guarded procedures for installation and migration

presentation.skill_body: knowledge boundary, invariants, retrieval map and tool vocabulary
presentation.reference_loading: one named reference at a time
presentation.project_facts: ProjectContextPack, AGENTS, SourceBindings and project knowledge

agent-collaboration-setup.domain: installation, project adoption and connection lifecycle
agent-collaboration-setup.description: Install, adopt, configure, validate, repair, upgrade, or remove ACS global services and project Management Roots, including local Harness MCP entries and remote web connection setup.

acs-project-context.domain: Project identity and authorized contact scope; Native capacity and source files retain their own authorities.
acs-project-context.description: Project, Root, Route and trusted caller context for ACS communication. Use when choosing a project, resolving contact visibility or continuing in another session.

acs-collaboration-model.domain: Communication among autonomous Agents. Their planning, engineering review and work acceptance remain external.
acs-collaboration-model.description: Stable AgentSlot contacts, natural messages, explicit replies and scoped team configuration in ACS. Use when contacting, configuring or handing context to another Agent.

acs-runtime-model.domain: Native receiving capacity and one authorized initiation, separate from message authorship and Agent reasoning.
acs-runtime-model.description: Actual Node, endpoint and Native Session bindings for ACS. Use when selecting receiving capacity, checking readiness or distinguishing configuration from real Native contact.

acs-continuity-recovery.domain: Communication persistence and bounded technical recovery; model understanding and work outcomes are external.
acs-continuity-recovery.description: Durable ACS Inbox/history, exact reply waiting and request identity across disconnects. Use when waiting, resuming communication or handling uncertain delivery.

acs-source-evidence.domain: Source provenance and actual file access. ACS messages carry references, not repository synchronization.
acs-source-evidence.description: Actual machine files, repository readers and source provenance for ACS communication. Use when sharing paths, choosing an authorized reader or verifying the bytes actually inspected.

acs-review-acceptance.domain: Engineering judgment outside ACS. The bridge transmits messages and authorized source references without a Review lifecycle.
acs-review-acceptance.description: External engineering review and acceptance using ACS communication and source evidence. Use when coordinating an independent review or reporting findings; decisions remain with external Agents.

acs-policy-governance.domain: Authentication and authority. Message text and a supplied reference cannot grant permission.
acs-policy-governance.description: Trusted Client and Slot caller bindings, project-scoped Grants and ACS management boundaries. Use when reasoning about who can contact, read or configure whom.

acs-web-collaboration.domain: Remote MCP entry, authentication and actual available receiving capabilities.
acs-web-collaboration.description: ACS communication through authenticated remote MCP and real project context. Use for web-hosted Agent access, reconnecting and distinguishing server files from client-local files.
